channel.title: The Cold Fusion Calendar — Upcoming Anniversaries
channel.description: Yearly anniversaries of milestones in cold fusion / LENR / energy science, looking 60 days ahead.

item.title: Apr 30: Three Lab Explosions in China (1991)
item.description: Zhang Xinwie et al. experience three explosions in their lab.

item.title: Apr 30: Swartz: Optimal Operating Point Characteristics (1998)
item.description: Key Experiment: Optimal Operating Point Characteristics by Mitchell Swartz.

item.title: May 1: Chubb Organizes First Cold Fusion APS Session (1989)
item.description: Scott Chubb organizes first session on cold fusion at an American Physical Society meeting.

item.title: May 1: APS Meeting Denounces Cold Fusion (1989)
item.description: Physicists at American Physical Society (APS) meeting hotly denounce the work of Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons.

item.title: May 2: Case Demonstrates D2 Gas-Loaded Cell (1998)
item.description: Leslie Case demonstrates deuterium gas-loaded metallic-catalyst cell.

item.title: May 3: Beaudette: 'Excess Heat' Book Released (2000)
item.description: Excess Heat How Cold Fusion Research Prevailed by Charles Beaudette is published. 2000. PDF: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/BeaudetteCexcessheat.pdf

item.title: May 3: CFN Podcast #011 — Dr. Vladimir Vysotskii: Biological Transmutations (2018)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 011 — Dr. Vladimir Vysotskii: Biological Transmutations and Deactivation of Radioactive Isotopes. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: https://coldfusionnow.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/A_CFN_011_Vladimir_Vysotskii.mp3

item.title: May 4: Bockris Confirms at Texas A&M (1989)
item.description: Third team at Texas A&M headed by John Bockris confirms Fleischmann-Pons Effect (FPE)

item.title: May 5: Storms Testifies Before U.S. Congress (1993)
item.description: Edmund Storms testifies before the U.S. House Subcommittee on Science, Space, and Technology. (See also CFN podcast #19: https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/)

item.title: May 7: India: Ten Teams Replicate Fleischmann-Pons (1989)
item.description: Mumbai's The Indian Post reports ten teams in India replicate the Fleischmann-Pons Effect (FPE)

item.title: May 8: F-Day at Electrochemical Society Meeting (1989)
item.description: F-day at Electrochemical Society Meeting.

item.title: May 9: Fleischmann & Pons at Electrochemical Society LA (1989)
item.description: Martin Fleischmann and Stanley Pons provide additional data at a meeting of the Electrochemical Society in Los Angeles, California.

item.title: May 10: Fleischmann, Pons & Hawkins Publish JEC Errata (1989)
item.description: Fleischmann, Pons, and Hawkins publish errata in Journal of Electroanalytical Chemistry.

item.title: May 12: Stan Szpak: Pd-D Co-deposition Method (1991)
item.description: Navy researcher Stan Szpak et al publish on a new method of initiating the reaction that he developed using electro-deposited palladium-deuteride. 1991 ..... in Journal Electroanalytical Chemistry.

item.title: May 13: Ruby Carat Founds Cold Fusion Now (2010)
item.description: In the midst of the BP Oil Catastrophe, Ruby Carat forms Cold Fusion Now to promote clean energy from cold fusion.

item.title: May 13: CFN Podcast #012 — Dr. Melvin Miles: The Heat-Helium Discovery (2018)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 012 — Dr. Melvin Miles: The Heat-Helium Discovery. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: http://www.coldfusionnow.com/podcast/Ruby-Carat-Melvin-Miles-Cold-Fusion-Now-012.mp3

item.title: May 15: Russian Glow-Discharge Cold Fusion Observation (1990)
item.description: A.B. Karabut, Ya.R. Kucherov, and I.V. Savvatimova present Cold Fusion Observation at Gas-Discharge Device Cathode.

item.title: May 18: Ten Teams Report FPE Replication (1989)
item.description: Ten teams report success replicating the FPE at cold fusion meeting at Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) near Mumbai, India.

item.title: May 19: Storms (1990)
item.description: Edmund Storms of Los Alamos National Lab (LANL) compiles survey of 16 successes in tritium detection, 15 in neutron detection, and 19 successes replicating the FPE. (See also CFN podcast #19: https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/)

item.title: May 19: ICCF-9: 9th International Cold Fusion Conference (2002)
item.description: ICCF-9 — International Conference on Cold Fusion held in Beijing, China. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/LiXZcondensedm.pdf

item.title: May 20: Storms Granted US 8,728,235 Cold Fusion Patent (2014)
item.description: Edmund Storms granted US 8,728,235 — Method and apparatus for cold fusion based on the Hydroton model of nuclear-active environments in palladium hydride. https://patents.google.com/patent/US8728235/en

item.title: May 21: ICCF-8: 8th International Cold Fusion Conference (2000)
item.description: ICCF-8 — International Conference on Cold Fusion held in Lerici, La Spezia, Italy. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/ScaramuzzVprocofthe.pdf

item.title: May 21: Journal of Condensed Matter Nuclear Science (2002)
item.description: The new field journal is named the Journal of Condensed Matter Nuclear Science (JCMNS). Archive: https://www.iscmns.org/CMNS/publications.htm

item.title: May 21: Arata Demonstrates Cold Fusion Cell Live (25x Return) (2008)
item.description: Yoshiaki Arata publicly demonstrates cold fusion cell generating 25x return.

item.title: May 22: Multi-Lab Confirmations of Fleischmann-Pons Effect (1989)
item.description: Case-Western Reserve, Texas A&M, U. of Florida, U. of Washington and the National Institute of Nuclear Physics at Frascati, Italy have all confirmed parts of the Fleischmann-Pons Effect.

item.title: May 22: Mallove Publishes 'Fire from Ice' (1991)
item.description: Fire from Ice: Searching for the Truth Behind the Cold Fusion Furor by Eugene Mallove is published. https://archive.org/details/firefromicesearc0000mall

item.title: May 22: Arata & Zhang: Solid Fusion Reactor Paper (2008)
item.description: Yoshiaki Arata of Osaka University and Yue-Chang Zhang of Shanghai Jiao Tong University publicly demonstrate cold fusion cell that generates 25 times energy return. 2008 ...for the public.

item.title: May 23: First LANL Workshop on Cold Fusion (1989)
item.description: The Workshop on Cold Fusion Phenomenon held at Los Alamos National Lab in New Mexico is the first cold fusion conference ever held.

item.title: May 25: Mexican Scientists Confirm Solid-State Fusion (1989)
item.description: A team of Mexican scientists report confirmation of solid-state fusion.

item.title: May 26: ICCF-26: 26th International Conference (CMNS) (2025)
item.description: ICCF-26 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Morioka, Japan. Proceedings / info: https://www.jcfrs.org/iccf26/

item.title: May 27: Google's $10M Cold Fusion Program (Nature paper) (2019)
item.description: “Revisiting the cold case of cold fusion” published in Nature by Berlinguette, Chiang, Munday, Schenkel, Fork, Koningstein, and Trevithick — Google's four-year, $10M multi-institution program (UBC, MIT, LBNL) revisits palladium hydride excess heat and develops new measurement techniques for the field. Nature 569: 581–588. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1256-6

item.title: May 28: First LANR/CF Colloquium at MIT (2005)
item.description: First LANR/CF Colloquium at MIT organized by Mitchell Swartz.

item.title: May 31: Gluck & Palibroda: Pd Thin-Foil Cold Fusion (1991)
item.description: Cold Nuclear Fusion in Thin Foils of Palladium by Peter Gluck and Evelina Palibroda reports finding neutrons.

item.title: Jun 1: Carnot: 'Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire' (1824)
item.description: Nicolas Leonard Sadi Carnot published first theoretical understanding of steam power in Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire.

item.title: Jun 3: American Nuclear Society Features LENR (1997)
item.description: American Nuclear Society Annual Meeting in Orlando, Florida features Low Energy Nuclear Reactions Panel session.

item.title: Jun 3: ICCF-21: 21st International Conference (CMNS) (2018)
item.description: ICCF-21 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Fort Collins, Colorado, USA. Proceedings / info: https://iccf21.com/

item.title: Jun 5: Arthur C. Clarke Calls Cold Fusion Greatest Scandal (1998)
item.description: Physicist and science fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke calls ignoring cold fusion “one of the greatest scandals in the history of science.”

item.title: Jun 5: CFN Podcast #024 — Dr. Sveinn Olafsson: Ultra-Dense Hydrogen & Rydberg Matter (2019)
item.description: Cold Fusion Now! Podcast Ep. 024 — Dr. Sveinn Olafsson: Ultra-Dense Hydrogen and Rydberg Matter. https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/ Audio: http://www.coldfusionnow.com/podcast/Ruby-Carat-Sveinn-Olafsson-Cold-Fusion-Now-024.mp3

item.title: Jun 7: Mallove Resigns from MIT News Office (1991)
item.description: Eugene Mallove formally resigns as MIT News Office Chief Science Writer.

item.title: Jun 7: Patent: US 5,318,675 — Patterson / CETI Electrolysis (1994)
item.description: James Patterson / Clean Energy Technologies Inc. (CETI) granted US 5,318,675 — System for the electrolysis of water using a porous matrix of micron-sized beads. https://patents.google.com/patent/US5318675A/en

item.title: Jun 9: ICCF-23: 23rd International Conference (CMNS) (2021)
item.description: ICCF-23 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Xiamen University, China (online & in-person). Proceedings / info: https://iccf23.iscmns.org/

item.title: Jun 11: CETI on ABC Good Morning America & Nightline (1997)
item.description: ABC-TV shows Good Morning America and NightLine feature Clean Energy Technology, Inc. (CETI) Patterson Power Cell on the same day.

item.title: Jun 11: Swartz LANR/CF Colloquium at MIT (2011)
item.description: LANR/CF Colloquium hosted by Mitchell Swartz held at MIT.

item.title: Jun 12: First Issue of Fusion Facts Published (1989)
item.description: First issue of Fusion Facts is published by Hal Fox announcing cold fusion is real and has commercial possibilities.

item.title: Jun 16: Fusion Facts: 242 Positive Papers from 23 Countries (1991)
item.description: Fusion Facts publishes a review of 242 positive papers from 23 countries.

item.title: Jun 18: Nagel Forms NUCAT Energy (2011)
item.description: David J. Nagel forms NUCAT Energy, LLC. (See also CFN Podcast #1: https://www.lackluster.org/cf/#2018-1-3)

item.title: Jun 19: First LENR/Transmutation Conference at Texas A&M (1995)
item.description: First Conference on Low Energy Nuclear Reactions (Transmutations) held at Texas A&M University.

item.title: Jun 23: BARC: Tritium Increase from Cold Fusion Cells (1989)
item.description: P.K. Iyengar and Mahadeva Srinivasan et al. measure four-fold increase of tritium from cold fusion cell. (See also CFN Podcast #7: https://www.lackluster.org/cf/#2018-3-23)

item.title: Jun 23: Cincinnati Group: LENT Radioactive Waste Remediation (1997)
item.description: The Cincinnati Group presents a process of radioactive waste remediation and offers a LENT-1 thorium activity reduction demonstration cell as a commercial product.

item.title: Jun 25: ICCF-13: 13th International Conference (CMNS) (2007)
item.description: ICCF-13 — International Conference on Condensed Matter Nuclear Science held in Sochi, Russia. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/BazhutovYNproceedinp.pdf

item.title: Jun 26: MIT 'Wake for Cold Fusion' Party (1989)
item.description: MIT Plasma Fusion Center holds Wake for Cold Fusion Party at 4PM claiming cold fusion is dead.

item.title: Jun 26: Storms & Talcott Detect Tritium at LANL (1989)
item.description: Edmund Storms and Carol Talcott from LANL detect tritium “in significant amounts” from Pd-D electrolytic cells. (See also CFN podcast #19: https://coldfusionnow.org/cfnpodcast/)

item.title: Jun 28: Bush & Eagleton Report Record Excess Heat (1991)
item.description: Robert Bush and Robert Eagleton report record amount of excess heat at ICCF-2.

item.title: Jun 29: ICCF-2: 2nd International Cold Fusion Conference (1991)
item.description: ICCF-2 — International Conference on Cold Fusion held in Como, Italy. Proceedings / info: http://lenr-canr.org/acrobat/BressaniTtheicc.pdf

item.title: Jun 29: DTRA Supports LENR Research (2007)
item.description: High Energy Science and Technology Assessment from U.S. Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA) supports cold fusion research.
